text: He sliced a frozen lake into blocks, and swore he'd sell it in August.
The whole town laughed at him.
Ice, in August? It'll be soup by June!
So he stacked it in a wooden shed, and buried it in sawdust.
You see, sawdust is packed with tiny pockets of trapped air, and trapped air barely passes heat.
The sun cooks the walls, but the cold stays locked inside.
So in August, when the whole town was melting, he opened the door,
and the first in line was the man who laughed when
